title: Rising inflation turns July Fed meeting into rate-hike showdown
summary: Rising inflation has turned the Federal Reserve’s July 28-29 meeting from an expected pause into a potential rate-hike showdown. After signs of easing — a cooler June CPI, lower oil prices and a steady labor market — renewed inflation pressures have made economists, traders and Fed watchers consider a rate increase plausible, heightening uncertainty for markets and borrowers.
content:
From thestreet.com

The Federal Reserve’s July 28-29 policymaking meeting on interest rates was, frankly, expected to be a snooze fest just a few weeks ago. Now, it’s going to be a humdinger. Economists, traders, and other Fed watchers were forecasting that the Federal Open Market Committee would vote to hold the benchmark Federal Funds Rate steady. This was due to a stabilizing labor market, a huge slide in oil prices, and a refreshing dip in the June Consumer Price Index, indicating a resilient U.S. economy that could take a beat from hawkish concerns that a tightening of policy was needed ASAP. Today, we’re looking at a coin flip between pausing and raising rates as evidence of rising inflation pressures has complicated the outlook.

Market participants who had penciled in a hold are now weighing fresh data and commentary that suggest inflation may be proving stickier than hoped. That uncertainty has elevated the stakes for the July meeting: a decision to hike would signal the Fed’s determination to tamp down inflation even at the risk of slowing growth, while a decision to hold would reflect confidence that recent cooling trends can continue without further tightening.

The outcome of the meeting will have immediate effects on financial markets, mortgage and loan rates, and broader economic expectations. Investors and consumers are watching closely for the Fed’s language on future action, the committee’s assessment of labor market resilience, and any guidance about how it will respond if inflation fails to ease.
